finding.trigger: Order work across independently executing participants.
finding.problem: Local timestamp comparisons do not establish causal dependencies.
finding.mechanism: Advance logical clocks along process/message edges; deterministic tie-breaks extend causal partial order.
finding.limits: Concurrent events can receive arbitrary order; example mutual exclusion requires live participants and message delivery.
finding.counterexample: Independent logical values 1 and 2 imply neither causality nor elapsed seconds.
finding.verification: Compare edge constraints against a recorded communication graph, including independent events.

not_adopted: Treat logical counters as global wall time
Infer happens-before from numeric timestamp inequality
Use the illustrative coordination algorithm as fault-tolerant consensus
Import physical-clock theorem without drift/communication bounds

current_primary_docs.title: TrueTime and external consistency
current_primary_docs.contract: Current external-consistency description applies to default/serializable isolation; repeatable-read has its separate semantics. MVCC enables nonblocking read snapshots.
current_primary_docs.limits: No current low-level lease proof, customer clock API, numeric uncertainty SLA or target-application behavior inferred.

current_primary_docs.title: Package time
current_primary_docs.read_by: delegated read-only runtime_clock_docs researcher and its Go documentation child
current_primary_docs.contract: Now carries wall and process-local monotonic readings. Add preserves both. After, Before, Equal, Compare and Sub use monotonic only when both operands retain it; otherwise they use wall time. Go == compares the stored representation including Location and the monotonic reading. Serialization, AddDate, Round, Truncate, In, Local and UTC strip monotonic information; Round(0) is an explicit example. Suspend may stop monotonic on some systems.
current_primary_docs.limits: No local Go installation tested. No cross-process/host preservation or durable epoch promised.
current_primary_docs.display_anomaly: A not-latest badge conflicted with the displayed edition; downloads/release history corroborated go1.27.1. Only the displayed verified edition is claimed.
current_primary_docs.contract_precision_review: Root independently rechecked official time documentation comparison paragraphs following reviewer feedback; no additional individual-method reading is claimed here.

current_primary_docs.title: Package context
current_primary_docs.read_by: delegated read-only runtime_clock_docs researcher and its Go documentation child
current_primary_docs.contract: Earlier parent deadline wins; WithTimeout constructs WithDeadline from time.Now().Add(timeout). Cancel signals termination but does not wait for completion.
current_primary_docs.limits: Documentation does not define wire propagation or synchronized clocks. Cancellation completion was not tested.

current_primary_docs.title: time — Time access and conversions
current_primary_docs.contract: Monotonic origin is undefined; documented clock is shared across processes. No shared host/reboot epoch follows. Linux CLOCK_BOOTTIME includes suspend; ordinary sleep is not a portable suspend guarantee. get_clock_info.adjustable excludes gradual NTP rate adjustment.
current_primary_docs.limits: No local Python clock, platform suspend or NTP behavior measured.

current_primary_docs.title: Coroutines and Tasks
current_primary_docs.contract: timeout_at uses loop clock and handles already-expired deadlines on a subsequent loop iteration. wait_for waits for cancellation and may exceed its allowance; wait does not cancel pending tasks on timeout.
current_primary_docs.limits: No event-loop/cancellation calls executed. A timeout signal does not prove a remote side effect stopped.

current_primary_docs.title: Event Loop
current_primary_docs.contract: loop.time is internal monotonic time; call_at uses the same reference. Timed callbacks may run up to one clock-resolution early.
current_primary_docs.limits: An epoch from time.time is not directly an event-loop deadline; scheduler lateness and suspend behavior not measured.
